ideas.title: Denoise item semantics with train-only transition consensus
ideas.motivation: Text or pretrained item embeddings can place substitutes far apart and near-duplicates together despite repeated user transitions; SIDs then fail to share useful prefixes for next-item generation.
ideas.novelty: Rather than feeding interaction samples into a quantizer or changing its geometry, this first constructs a bounded, item-level denoised embedding using only training sequences, then applies the existing SID tokenizer unchanged.
ideas.key_change: Build a symmetrized, popularity-corrected item transition graph from training sequences and mix each item embedding with a normalized average of its graph neighbors before the ordinary RQ-VAE fit/export.
ideas.specification: For each adjacent pair (i,j) in each training sequence increment C[i,j]. Let w_ij=(C[i,j]+C[j,i]) / ((deg_out(i)+1)^a (deg_out(j)+1)^a), with a=0.5; set P_ij=w_ij/sum_k w_ik. For each item with positive row sum, g_i=sum_j P_ij x_j, otherwise g_i=x_i. L2-normalize x_i and g_i, then x'_i=normalize((1-lambda)x_i+lambda*g_i), lambda in {0.1,0.3,0.5}. Fit and export the baseline tokenizer on x'_i; use no validation/test edges or item statistics. Compare with identical baseline configuration and select lambda only by the predeclared validation protocol.
ideas.cost_estimate: One training-sequence pass plus sparse graph aggregation O(E*d); memory O(E). Typically <5% additional Stage2 wall time, excluding unchanged tokenizer fitting.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: At least one lambda improves held-out next-item Recall@K/NDCG@K for a recommender trained on the resulting SIDs over baseline SIDs, while increasing train-only graph-neighbor embedding similarity of same-user transitions; otherwise reject.
ideas.risks: Popular hubs can cause oversmoothing; transition edges may encode navigational rather than semantic relations; sparse/short histories yield noisy estimates. Popularity correction and small lambda may not fully prevent these effects.

ideas.title: Assign IDs by bootstrap-consensus quantization
ideas.motivation: A small shift in initialization or sampled training items can move borderline products across code boundaries, making their semantic tokens unstable and depriving the generative recommender of repeatable prefix structure.
ideas.novelty: This targets tokenizer estimation uncertainty rather than adding another semantic modality, geometry, or sequential objective: train-only resampled tokenizer replicas estimate which item/code assignments are reliable, and only unstable assignments are regularized toward consensus.
ideas.key_change: Fit several lightweight tokenizer replicas on bootstrap resamples of training items, align replica code labels to a reference per codebook with Hungarian matching, then use cross-replica assignment frequencies as soft targets for a final standard tokenizer fit.
ideas.specification: Train B=5 replicas with the baseline architecture and hyperparameters, each sampling N training items with replacement and independent seed. For each level l, align replica code labels to replica 0 by maximum overlap of item assignments (Hungarian algorithm on the KxK overlap matrix). Define q_i,l,k=(1/B)sum_b 1[aligned_code_b(i,l)=k]. In the final tokenizer fit, retain the usual reconstruction/RQ loss and add L_cons=(gamma/(N*L))*sum_{i,l} KL(q_i,l || p_l(.|x_i)), where p is softmax of negative squared distances divided by fixed temperature tau=0.1 and gamma is selected from {0.01,0.1}; export the final model's ordinary hard assignments. All replicas and final fitting use training items only.
ideas.cost_estimate: Approximately 5 baseline tokenizer fits for replicas plus one final fit (about 6x Stage2 training compute); assignment alignment costs O(B*L*K^3), negligible at K=256 relative to fitting.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Across at least three seeds, consensus training reduces item assignment disagreement between independently fitted tokenizer seeds and improves validation next-item ranking versus the baseline at the same final-fit budget; if disagreement falls but validation ranking does not improve, discard.
ideas.risks: Code labels may not align cleanly where clusters split/merge; consensus can freeze a shared but poor local solution and reduce code utilization. Extra compute is substantial, and replica-derived targets can over-regularize rare items.
